In [[mathematics]], '''Aleksandrov–Clark (AC) measures''' are specially constructed [[Measure theory|measures]] named after the two [[mathematician]]s, [[Alexei Borisovich Aleksandrov|A. B. Aleksandrov]] and [[Douglas Clark (mathematician)|Douglas Clark]], who discovered some of their deepest properties. The measures are also called either Aleksandrov measures, Clark measures, or occasionally spectral measures.

AC measures are used to extract information about self-maps of the [[Unit disk|unit disc]], and have applications in a number of areas of [[complex analysis]], most notably those related to [[operator theory]]. Systems of AC measures have also been constructed for higher dimensions, and for the [[half-plane]].

==Construction of the measures==

The original construction of Clark relates to one-dimensional perturbations of compressed shift operators on subspaces of the [[Hardy space]]:

: <math>H^2(\mathbb{D},\mathbb{C}).</math>

By virtue of [[Beurling's theorem]], any shift-invariant subspace of this space is of the form
: <math>\theta H^2(\mathbb{D},\mathbb{C}),</math>

where <math>\theta</math> is an [[inner function]]. As such, any [[invariant subspace]] of the adjoint of the shift is of the form

: <math>K_\theta = \left(\theta H^2(\mathbb{D},\mathbb{C})\right)^\perp.</math>

We now define <math>S_\theta</math> to be the shift operator compressed to <math>K_\theta</math>, that is

: <math>S_\theta = P_{K_\theta} S|_{K_\theta}.</math>

Clark noticed that all the one-dimensional perturbations of <math>S_\theta</math>, which were also unitary maps, were of the form

: <math> U_\alpha (f) = S_\theta (f) + \alpha \left\langle f , \frac{\theta}{z} \right\rangle, </math>

and related each such map to a measure, <math>\sigma_\alpha</math> on the [[unit circle]], via the [[Spectral theorem]]. This collection of measures, one for each <math>\alpha</math> on the unit circle <math>^\mathbb{T}</math>, is then called the collection of AC measures associated with <math>\theta</math>.

==An alternative construction==

The collection of measures may also be constructed for any [[analytic function]] (that is, not necessarily an inner function). Given an analytic self map, <math>\phi</math>, of the unit disc, <math>^\mathbb{D}</math>, we can construct a collection of functions, <math>u_\alpha</math>, given by

:<math> u_\alpha(z) = \Re \left(\frac{\alpha + \varphi(z)}{\alpha - \varphi(z)}\right), </math>

one for each <math>^{\alpha\in\mathbb{T}}</math>. Each of these functions is positive and harmonic, so by Herglotz' Theorem each is the Poisson integral of some positive measure <math>\mu_\alpha</math> on <math>^\mathbb{T}</math>. This collection is the set of AC measures associated with <math>\varphi</math>. It can be shown that the two definitions coincide for inner functions.
